other_rules: Programme = compulsory reading material for attending students, supported by slides and notes; slides (incl. guest slides) are not study material (26/11).
Lessons 4 and 7: still in programme but low focus — 'there won't be very much work on four'; 'we won't be probably very focused on piracy and enforcement' (26/11).
Exam: closed books, Respondus; disconnecting = expulsion; paper backup; bring a pen (26/11).
Three sub-questions: Wennersten part 25%, Manderieux part 50% (~40 min), Seccombe part 25%; 60-80 min total (sometimes 90) (13/11, 26/11).
Answers in prose, short paragraphs, no bullet points, max ~3.5 pages; answer the question asked, not everything you know (13/11).
No contract analysis at the exam; it is an open question (05/11).
Same difficulty at every session (Dec, Jan, Feb, Sep); withdrawal allowed until the last minute; past attempts never count (26/11, 29/10).
Bonus up to 6: certificates 1.5 (EUIPO) or 3 (EPO), participation up to 2; grades never changed, 4 correctors (13/11, 26/11).
WIPO handbook figures may be outdated: book figures are fine, updated figures or extra case law also fine (26/11).
Programme is the same for classes 27 and 28; non-attending students study the book (26/11).
unclear: Which guest session is meant by 'what we did with Francesco Cerra is not in the exam as such' (26/11): likely the 19/11 guest (ip-18) — it is unclear whether the 09/10 Sobol guest (Boss case, ip-10 c2-c4) and the 30/10 EPO guest (ip-13) are also excluded. The general rule given is: guest slides are not study material, but the readings of those lessons remain.

Lesson 17: transcript says 'I know, uh, wrong convention, but of course, the TRIPS agreement' — possibly 'Rome Convention' was mentioned (in or out?); the Rome Convention reading (p. 314–319) status is ambiguous.

The 'I won't make any question at the exam on the AI inventions' line (30/10) is labelled Speaker 3 (the guest) but by context is the professor's interjection; either way AI inventorship is not exam material.
13/11 garbled example of cut material: 'something on, say, Harvard that we didn't do ... we won't have time to study the first license ... in China' — not identifiable.
Sekhon/Seccombe part (25% of exam): readings to be posted by him; not covered by the cut.
Not fully read: 30/10 morning, 09/10, rest of 08/10 and 05/11 transcripts (summaries contain no further exam-scope remarks).
